subject: Grouped Point Transects and estimating variance

messages.author: 3bbe9e00c88a70b2
messages.subject: Grouped Point Transects and estimating variance
parts:
Sorry if this has been addressed earlier by I could not find anything in
the archives.

If the spatial layout of point transects is such that they are grouped
(e.g., 6 points per group - where the distance among points in each
group is << than the distance among groups) then one might want to
estimate the variance using a bootstrap where the groups are selected
instead of individual points (see pp. 163-164 in Intro book).

My question is how to implement this in DISTANCE. I could see combining
data from each group and setting survey effort to 6 as one approach. But
doesn't this ignore some information about variability among points? It
seems to me it would be preferable to retain the information from
individual points but be able to select them by group in the bootstrap.

Maybe the solution is blindingly obvious... but I can't see it. Can
this be set up in DISTANCE or do I need to "trick" DISTANCE, such as by
creating strata that indicate the grouping and resample on strata?

Thanks,

Duane

messages.subject: Re: Grouped Point Transects and estimating variance
parts:
Duane, I would do exactly as you suggest - combine the data from the 6 poin=
ts. It is the clusters that are the independent sampling units, so assessi=
ng precision on the basis of variation among clusters is correct.

Of course, you could fit a spatial model to your count data, and then you c=
an retain the information from each individual point.

Steve Buckland
